subject: how exactly are files read into Shiny??

messages.author: 5117fd6c9c423ce1
messages.subject: how exactly are files read into Shiny??
parts:
Ok, guys,

I'm trying to get Shiny to read in a shapefile reactively, using rgdal to read it.  Rgdal needs the shapefile name to be passed to it  by breaking up the path and the root name of the shapefile w/o the extension.  I'm not figuring out how the filename gets parsed by Shiny when using inputFile?

ie, if in my server.R I have:

 mySHPdata <- reactive({
    inFile <- input$file1
   
    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)
    print(inFile)
    require(rgdal)
    return (
      readOGR(dirname(inFile), substr(basename(inFile),1,nchar(basename(inFile))-4))
     )
    })
   
assuming that inFile is the folder then the filename, that does not work.    I tried to print what inFile *is* to R, and I get :

name size type                                                                         datapath
1 ptsin.shp 1976      C:\\Users\\cynthart\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\Rtmp4gUu6i/f2e7f1c0c13d33bd35ac98d3/0

.. And I'm not gettin' hw to go about parsing that!  Can anyone help?  Thanks.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: how exactly are files read into Shiny??
parts:
inFile is a dataframe, in this case you want inFile$datapath although the extension and name will not be what you expect (it's just a tempfile). If you need it to be with the original filename, you'll need to copy or rename it.

From ?fileInput:

Whenever a file upload completes, the corresponding input variable is set to a dataframe. This dataframe contains one row for each selected file, and the following columns:

name

The filename provided by the web browser. This is not the path to read to get at the actual data that was uploaded (see datapath column).

size

The size of the uploaded data, in bytes.

type

The MIME type reported by the browser (for example, text/plain), or empty string if the browser didn't know.

datapath

The path to a temp file that contains the data that was uploaded. This file may be deleted if the user performs another upload operation.
